tools.name: git_add
tools.description: Stages changes in the Git repository for the next commit by adding file contents to the index (staging area). Can stage specific files/patterns or all changes (default: '.'). Returns the result as a JSON object.

path.description: Path to the Git repository. Defaults to the directory set via `git_set_working_dir` for the session; set 'git_set_working_dir' if not set.

files.description: Files or patterns to stage, defaults to all changes ('.')

tools.name: git_branch
tools.description: Manages Git branches. Supports listing (local, remote, all), creating, deleting (with force), renaming (with force), and showing the current branch. Returns results as a JSON object.

path.description: Path to the local Git repository. Defaults to the directory set via `git_set_working_dir` for the session; set 'git_set_working_dir' if not set.

branchName.description: The name of the branch (e.g., 'feat/new-login', 'main'). Required for 'create', 'delete', 'rename' modes.

newBranchName.description: The new name for the branch (e.g., 'fix/typo-in-readme'). Required for 'rename' mode.

startPoint.description: Optional commit hash, tag, or existing branch name (e.g., 'main', 'v1.0.0', 'commit-hash') to start the new branch from. Used only in 'create' mode. Defaults to HEAD.

force.description: Force the operation. Use -D for delete, -M for rename, -f for create (if branch exists). Use with caution, as forcing operations can lead to data loss.

all.description: List both local and remote-tracking branches. Used only in 'list' mode.

remote.description: Act on remote-tracking branches. Used with 'list' (-r) or 'delete' (-r).

tools.name: git_checkout
tools.description: Switches branches or restores working tree files. Can checkout branches, commits, tags, or specific file paths. Supports creating new branches and forcing checkout.

path.description: Path to the Git repository. Defaults to the directory set via `git_set_working_dir` for the session; set 'git_set_working_dir' if not set.

branchOrPath.description: The branch name (e.g., 'main'), commit hash, tag, or file path(s) (e.g., './src/file.ts') to checkout.

newBranch.description: Create a new branch named <new_branch> (e.g., 'feat/new-feature') and start it at <branchOrPath>.

force.description: Force checkout even if there are uncommitted changes (use with caution, discards local changes).

tools.name: git_cherry_pick
tools.description: Applies the changes introduced by existing commits. Supports picking single commits or ranges, handling merge commits, and options like --no-commit and --signoff. Returns results as a JSON object, indicating success, failure, or conflicts.

path.description: Path to the local Git repository. Defaults to the directory set via `git_set_working_dir` for the session; set 'git_set_working_dir' if not set.

mainline.description: Specify the parent number (starting from 1) when cherry-picking a merge commit.

noCommit.description: Apply the changes but do not create a commit.

signoff.description: Add a Signed-off-by line to the commit message.

tools.name: git_clean
tools.description: Removes untracked files from the working directory. Supports dry runs, removing directories, and removing ignored files. CRITICAL: Requires explicit `force: true` parameter for safety as this is a destructive operation. Returns results as a JSON object.

path.description: Path to the local Git repository. Defaults to the directory set via `git_set_working_dir` for the session; set 'git_set_working_dir' if not set.

force.description: REQUIRED confirmation to run the command. Must be explicitly set to true to perform the clean operation. If false or omitted, the command will not run.

dryRun.description: Show what would be deleted without actually deleting (-n flag).

directories.description: Remove untracked directories in addition to files (-d flag).

ignored.description: Remove ignored files as well (-x flag). Use with extreme caution.

tools.name: git_clear_working_dir
tools.description: Clears the session-specific working directory previously set by `git_set_working_dir`. Subsequent Git tool calls in this session will require an explicit `path` parameter or will default to the server's current working directory. Returns the result as a JSON object.

tools.name: git_clone
tools.description: Clones a Git repository from a given URL into a specified absolute directory path. Supports cloning specific branches and setting clone depth.

repositoryUrl.description: The URL of the repository to clone (e.g., https://github.com/cyanheads/git-mcp-server, git@github.com:cyanheads/git-mcp-server.git).

targetPath.description: The absolute path to the directory where the repository should be cloned.

branch.description: Specify a specific branch to checkout after cloning.

depth.description: Create a shallow clone with a history truncated to the specified number of commits.

quiet.description: Operate quietly. Progress is not reported to the standard error stream.

tools.name: git_commit
tools.description:
Commits staged changes to the Git repository index with a descriptive message. Supports author override, amending, and empty commits. Returns a JSON result.

**Commit Message Guidance:**
Write clear, concise commit messages using the Conventional Commits format: `type(scope): subject`.
- `type`: feat, fix, docs, style, refactor, test, chore, etc.
- `(scope)`: Optional context (e.g., `auth`, `ui`, filename).
- `subject`: Imperative, present tense description (e.g., "add login button", not "added login button").

I want to understand what you did and why. Use the body for detailed explanations, if necessary.

**Example Commit Message:**
```
feat(auth): implement password reset endpoint

- Adds the /api/auth/reset-password endpoint to allow users to reset their password via an email link. 
- Includes input validation and rate limiting.

Closes #123 (if applicable).
```

**Tool Options & Behavior:**
- Commit related changes logically. Use the optional `filesToStage` parameter to auto-stage specific files before committing.
- The `path` defaults to the session's working directory unless overridden. If `GIT_SIGN_COMMITS=true` is set, commits are signed (`-S`), with an optional `forceUnsignedOnFailure` fallback.

path.description: Path to the Git repository. Defaults to the directory set via `git_set_working_dir` for the session; set 'git_set_working_dir' if not set.

message.description: Commit message. Follow Conventional Commits format: `type(scope): subject`. Example: `feat(api): add user signup endpoint`

author.description: Overrides the commit author information (name and email). Use only when necessary (e.g., applying external patches).

amend.description: Amend the previous commit instead of creating a new one

forceUnsignedOnFailure.description: If true and signing is enabled but fails, attempt the commit without signing instead of failing.

filesToStage.description: Optional array of specific file paths (relative to the repository root) to stage automatically before committing. If provided, only these files will be staged.

tools.name: git_diff
tools.description: Shows changes between commits, commit and working tree, etc. Can show staged changes or diff specific files. An optional 'includeUntracked' parameter (boolean) can be used to also show the content of untracked files. Returns the diff output as plain text.

path.description: Path to the Git repository. Defaults to the directory set via `git_set_working_dir` for the session; set 'git_set_working_dir' if not set.

commit1.description: First commit, branch, or ref for comparison. If omitted, compares against the working tree or index (depending on 'staged').

commit2.description: Second commit, branch, or ref for comparison. If omitted, compares commit1 against the working tree or index.

staged.description: Show diff of changes staged for the next commit (compares index against HEAD). Overrides commit1/commit2 if true.

file.description: Limit the diff output to a specific file path.

includeUntracked.description: Include untracked files in the diff output (shows their full content as new files). This is a non-standard extension.

tools.name: git_fetch
tools.description: Downloads objects and refs from one or more other repositories. Can fetch specific remotes or all, prune stale branches, and fetch tags.

path.description: Path to the Git repository. Defaults to the directory set via `git_set_working_dir` for the session; set 'git_set_working_dir' if not set.

remote.description: The remote repository to fetch from (e.g., 'origin'). If omitted, fetches from 'origin' or the default configured remote.

prune.description: Before fetching, remove any remote-tracking references that no longer exist on the remote.

tags.description: Fetch all tags from the remote (in addition to whatever else is fetched).

tools.name: git_init
tools.description: Initializes a new Git repository at the specified path. If path is relative or omitted, it resolves against the session working directory (if you have set the git_working_dir). Can optionally set the initial branch name and create a bare repository.

initialBranch.description: Optional name for the initial branch (e.g., 'main'). Uses Git's default if not specified.

bare.description: Create a bare repository (no working directory).

quiet.description: Only print error and warning messages; all other output will be suppressed.

tools.name: git_log
tools.description: Shows commit logs for the repository. Supports limiting count, filtering by author, date range, and specific branch/file. Returns a JSON object containing a list of commit objects (`commits` array) by default. If `showSignature: true` is used, it returns a JSON object where the `commits` array is empty and the raw signature verification output is included in the `message` field.

path.description: Path to the Git repository. Defaults to the directory set via `git_set_working_dir` for the session; set 'git_set_working_dir' if not set.

maxCount.description: Limit the number of commits to output.

author.description: Limit commits to those matching the specified author pattern.

since.description: Show commits more recent than a specific date (e.g., '2 weeks ago', '2023-01-01').

until.description: Show commits older than a specific date.

branchOrFile.description: Show logs for a specific branch (e.g., 'main'), tag, or file path (e.g., 'src/utils/logger.ts').

showSignature.description: Show signature verification status for commits. Returns raw output instead of parsed JSON.

tools.name: git_merge
tools.description: Merges the specified branch into the current branch. Supports options like --no-ff, --squash, and --abort. Returns the merge result as a JSON object.

path.description: Path to the Git repository. Defaults to the directory set via `git_set_working_dir` for the session; set 'git_set_working_dir' if not set.

branch.description: The name of the branch to merge into the current branch.

commitMessage.description: Commit message to use for the merge commit (if required, e.g., not fast-forward).

noFf.description: Create a merge commit even when the merge resolves as a fast-forward (`--no-ff`).

squash.description: Combine merged changes into a single commit (`--squash`). Requires manual commit afterwards.

abort.description: Abort the current merge process (resolves conflicts).

tools.name: git_pull
tools.description: Fetches from and integrates with another repository or a local branch (e.g., 'git pull origin main'). Supports rebase and fast-forward only options. Returns the pull result as a JSON object.

path.description: Path to the Git repository. Defaults to the directory set via `git_set_working_dir` for the session; set 'git_set_working_dir' if not set.

remote.description: The remote repository to pull from (e.g., 'origin'). Defaults to the tracked upstream or 'origin'.

branch.description: The remote branch to pull (e.g., 'main'). Defaults to the current branch's upstream.

ffOnly.description: Use '--ff-only' to only allow fast-forward merges.

tools.name: git_push
tools.description: Updates remote refs using local refs, sending objects necessary to complete the given refs. Supports pushing specific branches, tags, forcing, setting upstream, and deleting remote branches. Returns the push result as a JSON object.

path.description: Path to the Git repository. Defaults to the directory set via `git_set_working_dir` for the session; set 'git_set_working_dir' if not set.

remote.description: The remote repository to push to (e.g., 'origin'). Defaults to the tracked upstream or 'origin'.

branch.description: The local branch to push (e.g., 'main', 'feat/new-login'). Defaults to the current branch.

remoteBranch.description: The remote branch to push to (e.g., 'main', 'develop'). Defaults to the same name as the local branch.

force.description: Force the push (use with caution: `--force-with-lease` is generally safer).

forceWithLease.description: Force the push only if the remote ref is the expected value (`--force-with-lease`). Safer than --force.

setUpstream.description: Set the upstream tracking configuration (`-u` or `--set-upstream`).

delete.description: Delete the remote branch (`--delete`). Requires `branch` to be specified. Use with caution, as deleting remote branches can affect collaborators.

tools.name: git_rebase
tools.description: Reapplies commits on top of another base tip. Supports starting a rebase (standard or interactive), continuing, aborting, or skipping steps in an ongoing rebase. Returns results as a JSON object.

path.description: Path to the local Git repository. Defaults to the directory set via `git_set_working_dir` for the session; set 'git_set_working_dir' if not set.

mode.description: Rebase operation mode: 'start' (initiate rebase), 'continue', 'abort', 'skip' (manage ongoing rebase).

upstream.description: The upstream branch or commit to rebase onto. Required for 'start' mode unless 'interactive' is true with default base.

branch.description: The branch to rebase. Defaults to the current branch if omitted.

interactive.description: Perform an interactive rebase (`-i`). 'upstream' can be omitted to rebase current branch's tracked upstream or use fork-point.

strategy.description: Specifies the merge strategy to use during rebase.

strategyOption.description: Pass a specific option to the merge strategy (e.g., 'ours', 'theirs' for recursive). Use with -X.

onto.description: Rebase onto a specific commit/branch instead of the upstream's base. Requires 'upstream' to be specified.

tools.name: git_remote
tools.description: Manages remote repositories (list, add, remove, show).

path.description: Path to the Git repository. Defaults to the directory set via `git_set_working_dir` for the session; set 'git_set_working_dir' if not set.

tools.name: git_reset
tools.description: Resets the current HEAD to a specified state. Supports different modes ('soft', 'mixed', 'hard', 'merge', 'keep') to control how the index and working tree are affected. Can reset to a specific commit. USE 'hard' MODE WITH EXTREME CAUTION as it discards local changes.

path.description: Path to the Git repository. Defaults to the directory set via `git_set_working_dir` for the session; set 'git_set_working_dir' if not set.

mode.description: Reset mode: 'soft' (reset HEAD only), 'mixed' (reset HEAD and index, default), 'hard' (reset HEAD, index, and working tree - USE WITH CAUTION), 'merge', 'keep'.

commit.description: Commit, branch, or ref to reset to. Defaults to HEAD (useful for unstaging with 'mixed' mode).

tools.name: git_set_working_dir
tools.description: Sets the default working directory for the current session. Subsequent Git tool calls within this session can use '.' for the `path` parameter, which will resolve to this directory. Optionally validates if the path is a Git repository (`validateGitRepo: true`). Can optionally initialize a Git repository with 'git init' if it's not already one and `initializeIfNotPresent: true` is set. Returns the result as a JSON object. IMPORTANT: The provided path must be absolute.

path.description: The absolute path to set as the default working directory for the current session. Set this before using other git_* tools.

validateGitRepo.description: Whether to validate that the path is a Git repository

initializeIfNotPresent.description: If true and the directory is not a Git repository, attempt to initialize it with 'git init'.

tools.name: git_show
tools.description: Shows information about Git objects (commits, tags, blobs, trees) based on a reference. Can optionally show the content of a specific file at that reference. Returns the raw output.

path.description: Path to the local Git repository. Defaults to the directory set via `git_set_working_dir` for the session; set 'git_set_working_dir' if not set.

ref.description: The object reference (commit hash, tag name, branch name, HEAD, etc.) to show.

filePath.description: Optional specific file path within the ref to show (e.g., show a file's content at a specific commit). If provided, use the format '<ref>:<filePath>'.

tools.name: git_stash
tools.description: Manages stashed changes in the working directory. Supports listing stashes, applying/popping specific stashes (with conflict detection), dropping stashes, and saving current changes to a new stash with an optional message. Returns results as a JSON object.

path.description: Path to the local Git repository. Defaults to the directory set via `git_set_working_dir` for the session; set 'git_set_working_dir' if not set.

message.description: Optional descriptive message used only for 'save' mode.

tools.name: git_status
tools.description: Retrieves the status of a Git repository. Returns a JSON object detailing the current branch, cleanliness, and changes. Staged and unstaged changes are grouped by status (e.g., Added, Modified), alongside lists of untracked and conflicted files.

path.description: Path to the Git repository. Defaults to the directory set via `git_set_working_dir` for the session; set 'git_set_working_dir' if not set.

tools.name: git_tag
tools.description: Manages Git tags. Supports listing existing tags, creating new lightweight or annotated tags against specific commits, and deleting local tags. Returns results as a JSON object.

path.description: Path to the local Git repository. Defaults to the directory set via `git_set_working_dir` for the session; set 'git_set_working_dir' if not set.

mode.description: The tag operation to perform: 'list' (show all tags), 'create' (add a new tag), 'delete' (remove a local tag).

tagName.description: The name for the tag. Required for 'create' and 'delete' modes. e.g., 'v2.3.0'.

message.description: The annotation message for the tag. Required and used only when 'mode' is 'create' and 'annotate' is true.

commitRef.description: The commit hash, branch name, or other reference to tag. Used only in 'create' mode. Defaults to the current HEAD if omitted.

annotate.description: If true, creates an annotated tag (-a flag) instead of a lightweight tag. Requires 'message' to be provided. Used only in 'create' mode.

tools.name: git_worktree
tools.description: Manages Git worktrees. Supports listing, adding, removing, moving, and pruning worktrees. Returns results as a JSON object.

path.description: Path to the local Git repository. Defaults to the directory set via `git_set_working_dir` for the session; set 'git_set_working_dir' if not set.

worktreePath.description: Path of the worktree. Required for 'add', 'remove', 'move' modes.

commitish.description: Branch or commit to checkout in the new worktree. Used only in 'add' mode. Defaults to HEAD.

newBranch.description: Create a new branch in the worktree. Used only in 'add' mode.

force.description: Force the operation (e.g., for 'add' if branch exists, or 'remove' if uncommitted changes).

detach.description: Detach HEAD in the new worktree. Used only in 'add' mode.

newPath.description: The new path for the worktree. Required for 'move' mode.

verbose.description: Provide more detailed output. Used in 'list' and 'prune' modes.

dryRun.description: Show what would be done without actually doing it. Used in 'prune' mode.

expire.description: Prune entries older than this time (e.g., '1.month.ago'). Used in 'prune' mode.

tools.name: git_wrapup_instructions
tools.description: Provides a standard Git wrap-up workflow. This involves reviewing changes with `git_diff`, updating documentation (README, CHANGELOG), and making logical, descriptive commits using the `git_commit` tool. The tool's response also includes the current `git status` output. You should set the working directory using `git_set_working_dir` before running this tool.

acknowledgement.description: Acknowledgement that you have permission (implicit allowed, explicit preferred) from the user to initiate this tool. Must be "Y" or "Yes" (case-insensitive).

updateAgentMetaFiles.description: If set to 'Y' or 'Yes', include an extra instruction to review and update agent-specific meta files like .clinerules or claude.md if present. Only use this if the user explicitly requested it.
